title: HPE is in talks to buy Nutanix: Report
summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) is reportedly in discussions to acquire cloud computing firm Nutanix. This potential acquisition could establish HPE as a dominant force in the cloud computing market and allow it to cross-sell growth-oriented software to its extensive customer base. title: Vodafone Picks Dubber for UK and European Business Strategy
summary: Vodafone Group PLC has partnered with Dubber, a Melbourne-based conversational intelligence and unified recording company, to deliver direct recording and AI services across its mobile networks for business customers in the UK and Europe, starting with Germany. This collaboration will leverage Dubber's platform to provide enhanced compliance and data insights across mobile and UC services, including RingCentral, Cisco Webex, and Microsoft Teams. title: Salesforce shares tumble after surprise exit of co-CEO Taylor
summary: Salesforce Inc (CRM.N) shares fell by about 10% after co-CEO Bret Taylor's unexpected departure, raising concerns about the company's co-CEO leadership model and slowing revenue growth. This exit prompted at least 17 brokerages to cut their price targets on the stock, with analysts noting it as a significant blow given Taylor's leadership role in product development. Taylor's departure comes after just one year in the co-CEO role, leaving co-founder Marc Benioff as the sole top boss.

summary: Rackspace Technology, a major cloud and email hosting provider, announced a ransomware attack is responsible for a widespread outage that has kept some customers from their email inboxes since Friday. title: AWS, Google, Microsoft and Oracle all get a piece of the Pentagon's $9B JWCC cloud computing contract
summary: The Pentagon has awarded Amazon Web Services, Microsoft, Google, and Oracle shared portions of a $9 billion Joint Warfighting Cloud Capability (JWCC) contract, which will run through 2028. This multi-vendor approach replaces the previously controversial single-award JEDI contract and aligns with industry best practices of using multiple cloud providers for resilience and cost management. Analysts view this distributed award as a positive step, promoting competition and allowing the DOD to leverage the best capabilities of each cloud provider.

title: Oracle jumps into payments for retailers
summary: Oracle has expanded its services for retailers to include in-store payment acceptance, offering tap-to-pay capabilities for various payment methods like debit, credit, Apple, Google, and Samsung digital wallets. Oracle aims to provide a more stable and cost-effective "payment to processing" solution, integrating it with their existing hardware and cloud-based software for inventory and staff management.

title: Meta Platforms must face advertisers' class action, US appeals court says
summary: A U.S. appeals court ruled that Meta Platforms must face a class action lawsuit from advertisers who claim the company overcharged them by inflating the "potential reach" metric for ads on Facebook and Instagram. Advertisers allege that this metric measured social media accounts rather than actual people, leading to an overestimation of potential viewers by up to 400%. The court also decertified a separate class seeking injunctive relief but allowed the damages class action to proceed, which could potentially result in over $7 billion in damages.

summary: The article discusses how the rapid growth of AI is leading to unprecedented demand for electricity and infrastructure, similar to how energy-efficient lightbulbs ultimately increased overall energy consumption. The author suggests that investments in grid modernization, power generation, and innovative energy solutions like small modular nuclear reactors (SMRs) are crucial to meet this surging demand.

title: Taiwanese chipmaker TSMC announces new $100B investment in US
summary: Taiwanese chip giant TSMC announced a new $100 billion investment in the U.S. for three additional advanced semiconductor manufacturing plants, bringing their total commitment to $165 billion. CEO C.C. Wei credited President Donald Trump's vision for these investments, which will include an R&D center in Arizona. This expansion follows TSMC's existing $65 billion commitment under the CHIPS and Science Act and comes amidst discussions about avoiding potential U.S. tariffs on foreign-made chips.
